clue.text: Small girl and boy heard to amuse, Hegelian style

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

indicators.note: says the word for amusing is spoken, and its sound is what goes in the grid

parts.note: to tickle someone is to amuse them

explanation.surface: Some odd little family entertainment carried out in the manner of the German philosopher Hegel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns TICKLE into its sound-alike ending TICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegel's philosophy proceeds by thesis, antithesis and synthesis, a method known by this adjective.

clue.text: Having no choice? Send if worried to cattle farm on other side

indicators.note: worried means agitated or disturbed, so the letters of send if are shaken up

parts.note: a ranch is a cattle farm

indicators.note: the letters of side are made into an other arrangement of them

explanation.surface: Someone unsure about being sent off to a cattle farm across the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' makes DISENF from SEND IF; 'other' makes ISED from SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing the vote means losing your say, the electoral choice; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Early hours for the Guardian's affair

parts.note: the newspaper speaking of itself says 'our'

explanation.surface: A romance carried on in the small hours by the newspaper staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for love is used in English for a love affair, often a secret one.

clue.text: I'm on the table with disgraced peer and sacked general

indicators.note: disgraced means thrown into disorder, so the letters of peer are scrambled
sacked suggests being knocked about and ransacked, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Something at a dinner shares the table with a disgraced lord and a dismissed general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disgraced' makes EPER from PEER; 'sacked' makes GNE from GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: This ornamental branched centrepiece holds fruit or flowers in the middle of a dining table.

clue.text: Maximum speed ahead?

parts.note: top means maximum, as in top speed
a knot is a unit of speed at sea

explanation.surface: Full speed in front?
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead' is read as 'on a head', where this tuft of hair is tied.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuft or bun of hair tied up on the crown sits on the head, a loose definition.

clue.text: 19's son-in-law makes crown available to everyone

indicators.note: made available means put into new usable form, so the letters of crown are rearranged

explanation.surface: A royal relative by marriage makes the crown open to the whole populace.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is LEAR; in Shakespeare's play his daughter Regan is married to the Duke of this title. CORNWALL is England's south-western county.
explanation.definitionFit: In King Lear, Regan's husband is a duke named after this English county.

clue.text: See yourself giving advice to driver

definitions.meaning: a motorist is told to check the rear-view glass before manoeuvring

explanation.surface: Advice that could be self-help or driving instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both viewing your reflection and checking behind before a car manoeuvre.

clue.text: Ornament for gun dogs?

definitions.meaning: a woolly ball decorating a hat
a quick-firing anti-aircraft gun of the world wars
two Pomeranian dogs, each a pom

explanation.surface: Asking whether a decoration is meant for gun dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a woolly ball decoration, a rapid-firing cannon, and jokingly a pair of Pomeranians.

clue.text: British king in painting by father of chariot racer?

parts.note: Ben means 'son of', so the chariot racer Ben-Hur's father is Hur

explanation.surface: A British monarch shown in a picture by the father of an ancient charioteer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben-Hur, the chariot-racing hero of the novel and film, is literally 'son of Hur'.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary king of the Round Table is the most famous king of ancient Britain.

clue.text: Riding wild horse towards land

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so the letters of horse are thrown about

explanation.surface: A rider on a bucking horse heading for land.
explanation.definitionFit: An onshore wind blows from sea to coast, in the direction of land.

clue.text: Speaker's chamber?

parts.note: not the room of the Speaker of the House, but a room for speaking: from French parler, to speak

explanation.surface: Asking about the private room of the House of Commons Speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting room was originally a room set aside for conversation, from the French for talking.

clue.text: See 21
A question of pronunciation for one doing spelling?

indicators.note: the word for a spell-caster is to be said aloud, giving a same-sounding word

explanation.surface: A query about how to say a word, posed to a speller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling' is not about letters but about casting spells.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an interrogative word asking for a choice among options.

clue.text: King of 5 associated with 8 achieves fame

definitions.meaning: the legendary ruler of Cornwall (5) in the Arthurian (8) tales, uncle of Tristan
distinction, as in a person of note

explanation.surface: A Cornish king linked to Arthur becomes renowned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'achieves' is a link; the second sense is fame, as in 'a man of note'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cornish king of the Tristan and Iseult legend; and renown, as in someone of distinction.

clue.text: Exposer of vagrant in love with tart

indicators.note: vagrant means wandering, so these letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: Someone who unmasks a tramp romancing a loose woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vagrant' is the anagram signal on IN LOVE and TART; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan or air shaft lays a room open to fresh air, so it exposes it.

clue.text: What a pity loved one's expensive!

explanation.surface: Regretting that a sweetheart costs so much.
explanation.definitionFit: The repeated exclamation expresses regret or mild dismay, like 'oh no'.

clue.text: Pale powder covers fairy king with itchy feet

indicators.note: says the powder word wraps round the fairy king

parts.note: the Erl-king is the elf king of German legend

explanation.surface: Ghostly white powder dusting an elf king who cannot stay still.
explanation.walkthrough: The Erl-king is the elf king of German legend, known from Goethe's poem and Schubert's song.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchy feet is an idiom for restless urge to travel.

clue.text: Hurts that may get us down?

indicators.note: get here means make into, so the letters of us down are made into something new

explanation.surface: Injuries that may depress us.
explanation.definitionFit: Injuries are hurts, the noun sense.

clue.text: Clearly a convenience for Armstrong's partner, say

indicators.note: tells us the phrase is spoken aloud and the sound is entered

parts.note: a loo (convenience) for Siddeley, partner in the motor and aero firm Armstrong Siddeley

explanation.surface: Plainly, a toilet for the astronaut's colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: Armstrong suggests Neil or Louis, but it is Armstrong Siddeley, the old British car and aero-engine maker.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak clearly is to speak in a lucid way, an adverb synonym.

clue.text: Raise one lily as required by oriental warriors

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the pieces upward, so read them bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Lift a single lily, as Japanese warriors demand.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the hereditary military class of feudal Japan.

clue.text: British king, one on field

annotationWithheld.why: British king, one on field (4): blog parses LEA (field) + R, but the R needs 'king', which is already in the definition 'British king'; one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Having nasal problems allegedly, with plenty of space

indicators.note: allegedly means 'so it is said', so the word for spacious is spoken

explanation.surface: Someone with blocked sinuses is supposedly roomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is watery discharge from nose or eyes, so a rheumy person is runny-nosed.

clue.text: Behead reformer and wait, not losing temper with British king

indicators.note: remove the head letter of the word for the reformer

parts.note: pend is to wait or hang
to lose your rag is to lose your temper, so not losing it you keep your rag on

explanation.surface: Decapitate a Protestant churchman and stay patient, keeping calm in the presence of an ancient British monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'lose your rag' is British slang for losing your temper.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary British king who was father of Arthur.

clue.text: British king taking much of Wales by almost direct route

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letters dropped

parts.note: Cymru is the Welsh name for Wales

indicators.note: one letter short of the full word

parts.note: a beeline is the straightest route

explanation.surface: A monarch annexing most of Wales by a nearly straight path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much of' cuts RU from CYMRU; 'almost' cuts an E from BEELINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary British king of Shakespeare's late romance.

clue.text: Jewish ascetic docked at German city

indicators.note: a tail cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect

explanation.surface: A hermit from Judea moors at a German port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' sounds nautical but means cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: The industrial city in the Ruhr region of Germany.

clue.text: Stretch performed without shooter

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the performed word goes round the gun

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: Doing exercises without a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell or expand outward is to stretch, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Stand having wrong sort to drink

indicators.note: wrong means badly set out, so the letters of sort go astray

explanation.surface: A platform for the wrong kind of drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform for a speaker is a stand.

clue.text: Associate of crown, Michael who directed the successful Equus?

parts.note: Royal Crown Derby is a porcelain maker
Michael Winner was a British film director

explanation.surface: A connection of the crown and the director of the play about a horse-blinding boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Equus is Latin for horse; the race is the Derby at Epsom, Britain's top flat race.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that wins the Epsom flat race is successful in the classic sense.
